title: Professional Editorial Standards (2024 edition)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The four stages of editing (structural, stylistic, copy editing, proofreading) as a professional body defines them; the 2024 edition replaced the 2016 edition.

title: The Chicago Manual of Style Online
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The current edition is the 18th (copyright 2024); the online edition is offered by subscription with a free trial.

title: A to Z style guide
publisher: GOV.UK Content and publishing guidance (Government Digital Service)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. UK government house style: abbreviations without full stops, dates as 2 June, 'to' in ranges, sentence case, 'and' not '&', bullet rules, no italics, bold only for interface elements. The old gov.uk/guidance/style-guide URL now redirects here (seen 6 Nov 2026).

title: Use clear language
publisher: GOV.UK Content and publishing guidance (Government Digital Service)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plain English is mandatory on GOV.UK; split sentences over 25 words; no more than 5 sentences per paragraph; active voice; short words; watch -ion and -ment words; must, need and can; specialists prefer plain English too; 1 in 6 adults in England have very poor literacy skills.

title: Write content to meet user needs
publisher: GOV.UK Content and publishing guidance (Government Digital Service)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Identify the user need before writing; publish only what meets it; guidance should hold only what a person needs to finish the task.

title: Welcome: Microsoft Writing Style Guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The online guide replaces the Microsoft Manual of Style and covers voice, bias-free communication and global communication; page metadata shows an update on 15 October 2026.

title: Top 10 tips for Microsoft style and voice
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Fewer words, write like you speak, contractions, get to the point, sentence-style capitals, no end punctuation in headings, serial (Oxford) comma, one space after full stops, no spaces around em dashes, start with a verb and cut 'there is'.

title: Google developer documentation style guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Order of precedence: project style, then this guide, then Merriam-Webster for spelling, Chicago (17th edition named) for non-technical style and Microsoft for technical style; it calls itself guidelines, not rules, and asks for consistency when departing from it.

title: Interinstitutional Style Guide
publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The EU's editorial conventions: legal act structure, conventions common to all languages, and English house rules (punctuation, spelling, numbers and dates, gender-neutral language).

title: Mailchimp Content Style Guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A real company's public house style guide covering voice and tone, grammar and mechanics, accessibility, legal content and a word list; licensed CC BY-NC 4.0; page shows copyright 2023.

title: Plain language guide series
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Four guides (principles, writing, design and testing for understanding); says the content is adapted from PlainLanguage.gov. The old plainlanguage.gov/guidelines URL redirects here (seen 6 Nov 2026).

title: Principles of plain language
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plain language means people can find, understand and use information; write for your audience; not dumbing down; references the Plain Writing Act of 2010.

title: Writing for understanding
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Active voice shows who does what; present tense; turn hidden verbs (nominalisations) back into verbs; shorter words and sections.

title: Politics and the English Language (George Orwell, Horizon, April 1946)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Orwell's six rules for clear writing, summarised in our own words in knowledge.md.

title: How Users Read on the Web (Jakob Nielsen, 1997)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 79% of test users scanned and 16% read word by word; concise text 58%, scannable layout 47%, objective language 27% and all three 124% better usability than the promotional version. Dated 30 September 1997.

title: PIAAC 2023 U.S. national results
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 28% of US adults aged 16 to 65 scored at Level 1 or below in literacy in 2023, up from 19% in 2017 (report NCES 2024-202).

title: Get your document's readability and level statistics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. How to show Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level in Word; Microsoft suggests 60 to 70 reading ease and about grade 7.0 to 8.0 for most documents; both tests use sentence length and syllables per word.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
supports: Opened with WebFetch. WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation dated 12 December 2024.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.1.5: Reading Level
supports: Opened with WebFetch. SC 3.1.5 is Level AAA: text above lower secondary education level needs supplemental content or a simpler version; lower secondary means 7 to 9 years of school (UNESCO ISCED).

title: Inclusive language: words to use and avoid when writing about disability
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 'Disabled people' not 'the disabled'; avoid 'suffers from' and 'wheelchair-bound'; let people self-identify. Updated 17 June 2026.

title: Track changes in Word
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Turning tracking on for everyone or only your own edits, locking tracking, accepting and rejecting changes, Simple Markup and All Markup views.

title: Suggest edits in Google Docs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Suggesting mode, explaining a change with a comment, accepting or rejecting one or all suggestions; people with comment or edit permission can suggest.

title: Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors (ICMJE Recommendations)
publisher: International Committee of Medical Journal Editors
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Four authorship criteria; chatbots cannot be authors; disclose AI use (writing help in acknowledgments, analysis in methods); writing assistance, language editing and proofreading alone do not earn authorship and should be acknowledged. Page shows copyright 2026; no update date given.

title: Generative AI policies for journals
supports: Opened with WebFetch. June 2026 update: declare AI use; basic grammar and spelling checks need no declaration but substantive rewriting does; AI cannot be an author; reviewers must not upload manuscripts to AI tools; rules on AI images.

title: EQUATOR Network: Enhancing the QUAlity and Transparency Of health Research
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Reporting guidelines by study type: CONSORT and SPIRIT (trials), STROBE (observational), PRISMA (systematic reviews), STARD, TRIPOD+AI, COREQ, SRQR, CARE, ARRIVE, SQUIRE, CHEERS.

title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers (Liang, Yuksekgonul, Mao, Wu and Zou, 2023)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Detectors often misclassify non-native English writing as AI-generated while classifying native writing correctly; simple prompting can get round detectors.

title: Suggested minimum rates
publisher: Chartered Institute of Editing and Proofreading (CIEP)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Suggested minimum hourly rates for 2026-27 from 1 March 2026: proofreading GBP 31.92, copyediting GBP 37.11, substantial editing, rewriting and development editing GBP 42.66, project management GBP 46.19.
